<div class="ipcc-654-wrap" role="region" aria-label="Climate-related hazards and their consequences for electricity systems">
<table class="ipcc-654">
<thead>
<tr>
<th scope="col">Hazard</th>
<th scope="col">Expected influence of climate change</th>
<th scope="col">Potential electricity-system consequences</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th scope="row"><span class="hazard-label">Extreme winds</span></th>
<td class="climate-signal"><span class="direction">Uncertain change in extreme winds</span><span class="qualification">Evidence that extreme winds will increase or in frequency or intensity is limited (except for tropical cyclones for which intensity is expected to increase). </span></td>
<td class="system-effect">Mechanical failure or collision of lines; damage to electricity infrastructure, including utility-scale wind and solar facilities; and additional network stress when storm exposure coincides with high demand.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th scope="row"><span class="hazard-label">Wildfire</span></th>
<td class="climate-signal"><span class="direction">Risk expected to increase </span><span class="qualification">It is very likely that climate change has already increased the likelihood and severity of extreme fire weather @Attribution2026 . </span></td>
<td class="system-effect">Damage to lines, substations and vegetation corridors; fire-related faults; and interruptions to electricity service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th scope="row"><span class="hazard-label">Lightning</span></th>
<td class="climate-signal"><span class="direction">Probable increase</span><span class="qualification">Atmospheric conditions are expected to become more favorable to thunderstom development.</span></td>
<td class="system-effect">Wildfire ignition, electrical arcing and simultaneous failures of multiple circuits or pieces of equipment, potentially resulting in wider outages.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th scope="row"><span class="hazard-label">Snow and ice</span></th>
<td class="climate-signal"><span class="direction">Overall risk expected to decline</span><span class="qualification">Sporadic acute cold, snow and icing events will remain possible.</span></td>
<td class="system-effect">Mechanical loading and collapse of lines; cascading outages; flashovers caused by wet snow; and icing impacts on wind turbines.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th scope="row"><span class="hazard-label">Extreme heat</span></th>
<td class="climate-signal"><span class="direction">Increase in both daily minimum and daily maximum temperatures</span></td>
<td class="system-effect">  Increased electricity demand and higher peak loads from cooling; reduced power-transfer capacity of overhead lines; and thermal stress on transformers, electrical equipment and supporting communication systems. These effects can occur simultaneously, reducing operating margins when the electricity system
  is under greatest demand.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th scope="row">
  <span class="hazard-label">
    <span>River flooding</span>
  </span>
</th>
<td class="climate-signal">
  <span class="direction">Changes vary by river basin and region</span>
  <span class="qualification">
    River-flood risk depends on changes in precipitation, snowmelt, river flow,
    soil moisture and other catchment conditions.
  </span>
</td>
<td class="system-effect">
  Inundation or damage to substations, generating facilities and other
  electricity assets located in river floodplains, potentially interrupting
  electricity generation, transmission or distribution.
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<th scope="row">
  <span class="hazard-label">
    <span>Heavy precipitation and pluvial flooding</span>
  </span>
</th>
<td class="climate-signal">
  <span class="direction"> Expected to increase</span>
  <span class="qualification">
    More intense rainfall can exceed local drainage capacity.
  </span>
</td>
<td class="system-effect">
  Local inundation of substations, underground cable systems and other
  low-lying electrical equipment where intense rainfall exceeds drainage
  capacity, potentially causing localized electricity outages.
</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<th scope="row">
  <span class="hazard-label">
    <span>Coastal flooding</span>
  </span>
</th>
<td class="climate-signal">
  <span class="direction">Exposure expected to increase</span>
  <span class="qualification">
    Sea-level rise increases the frequency and severity of extreme coastal
    water levels and can amplify flooding associated with storm surge.
  </span>
</td>
<td class="system-effect">
 Inundation or damage to coastal power plants, substations, underground cable
  systems and other low-lying electricity infrastructure during coastal
  flooding and storm surge, potentially disrupting generation, transmission
  and distribution.
</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>

::: {.ipcc-table-caption}
**Climate-related hazards and their potential consequences for electricity systems.** The expected influence of climate change differs among hazards and remains uncertain in some cases. Electricity-system impacts depend on asset exposure, infrastructure design, system configuration, and the coincidence of hazards with operational stresses such as high electricity demand. *Based on Section 6.5.4 of* @IPCC_2022_WGIII_Ch06, *with information on projected changes in climatic impact-drivers from* @IPCC_2021_WGI_Ch12.
:::
